Under this reading, when both conditions are met, the agent is required to issue the refund; failing to do so constitutes a violation. This differs from existing readings which treat the exception as permissive (may refund) rather than directive (must refund).

hypotheses.basis: Section A's 'otherwise non-refundable' combined with 'Several fare rules follow' can be read as a closed-world constraint: the only path to a full refund is through the enumerated fare rules, and when Section K's conditions are satisfied the refund is mandatory. This produces both a prohibition on refunding outside the conditions and an obligation to refund within them. Unlike reading 2 (open-ended), this treats the exception set as exhaustive; unlike readings 1 and 3, it adds the mandatory-action dimension.
